source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

54081.t:
Raleigh County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved sharply toward the Democrats. Capito beat Anderson 10,570 to 5,119, a 34-point margin, down from Trump's 54-point margin over Harris in 2024. That 21-point shift almost exactly matches the typical West Virginia county (+20) and the state as a whole (+22), and is larger than the typical move nationally (+14). Every county in the state moved left. Nearby comparisons ranged from Mercer (+17) to Wayne (+25).

Only 16,196 votes were cast, 52% of the 2024 total. With turnout that low, the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from Trump voters staying home.

54093.t:

That is close to the typical West Virginia county, which moved 20 points, and the state as a whole, which moved 22. Every county in the state moved left.

Turnout fell sharply: 2,541 votes were cast, about 70% of the 2024 total. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar small counties varied, from Summers at 14 points to Pocahontas at 22.

Turnout fell sharply: 3,319 votes, 44% of the 7,565 cast in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among counties with similar 2024 results and size, Mingo moved 24 points, Ritchie 16 and Doddridge 15.

54021.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Republican Capito beat Democrat Anderson in Gilmer County by 37 points, 1,039 votes to 463, down from Trump's 57-point margin in 2024. That 20-point shift toward the Democrats matches the typical West Virginia county, all 55 of which moved left, and exceeds the national typical move of 14 points. Gilmer ranks 28th of 55 in the state by size of move.

Only 1,560 votes were cast, about two-thirds of the 2,344 cast in 2024 and the second-fewest of any county in the state, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Pleasants moved 19 points, Hardy 15 and Pendleton 12.

54069.t:
Ohio County moved toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Anderson and Capito, but by less than any other county in West Virginia. Trump carried it by 26 points in 2024; Capito carried it by 15, 6,836 votes to 5,065, with 99% of the expected vote counted. That shift of about 11 points ranks 55th of 55 counties in a state where every county moved left, the typical one by 20 points and the state as a whole by 22. Comparable counties moved further: Marion by 23 points, Jefferson by 21 and Cabell by 19.

Only 12,152 votes were cast, 65% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

54055.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Anderson and Capito, Mercer County stayed firmly Republican but by less than in 2024. Trump carried it by 57 points; Capito won it by 40, 8,399 votes to 3,492, a 17-point move toward the Democrats. With 99% of the expected vote counted, the figures are close to final.

Only 12,300 votes were cast, 52% of the 23,584 in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Every West Virginia county moved left, the typical one by 20 points, and Mercer ranks 44th of 55. Counties with similar 2024 margins moved further: Preston and Mason by 23 points each, Jackson by 19.

54101.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Webster County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 19 points toward the Democrats. Capito beat Anderson 1,209 to 408, a margin of 48 points, down from Trump's 67-point margin over Harris in 2024. With 99% of the expected vote counted, the result is close to final.

Turnout was much lower: 1,685 votes, 56% of the 2024 total of 2,998. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Every West Virginia county moved left, the typical one by 20 points, and Webster ranks 34th of 55. Similar small counties moved about as much: Wirt 18 points, Tyler 16 and Calhoun 20. Statewide, Capito won by 20 points, after Trump carried the state by 42.

54107.t:
Wood County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved about 18 points toward the Democrats. Shelley Capito (R) beat Rachel Anderson (D) here by 25 points, 13,818 votes to 8,139, after Trump carried the county by 43 points in 2024. Turnout was much lower: 22,662 votes, 61% of the 2024 total. With that big a drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Every West Virginia county moved left. Wood's shift was smaller than the typical county's 20 points and ranked 42nd of 55, though it cast the fourth-most votes. Similar counties moved more: Harrison by 21 points, Putnam by 20 and Greenbrier by 19.

54075.t:
Pocahontas County swung toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Anderson and Capito. Trump carried it by 50 points in 2024; Capito won it by 28, 1,446 votes to Anderson's 791. That is a 22-point move, slightly more than the state's own 22-point shift to Capito's 20-point statewide win, and above the typical West Virginia county's 20 points. All 55 counties in the state moved left. Among similar counties, Tucker moved 21 points, Braxton 19 and Summers 14.

Only 2,315 votes were cast, 59% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.
